source.quote: Asana uses OAuth 2.0 for secure user authorization.

oauthAppCreation.where: Asana developer console: Create new app, then OAuth > Permission scopes

source.quote: To do so, first visit the developer console and select Create new app

reviewGate.trigger: Review is only needed to publish the app in the Asana App Directory (and for apps with app components, a security and QA review). An OAuth app works without review.

source.quote: Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token.

moreSources.quote: If you're building an internal tool or testing your integration, you can create and use an OAuth app without submitting it for review.

approvalWait.stated: Initial response on a submission within one week; longer for complex apps and apps with app components

source.quote: We aim to provide an initial response on app submissions within one week.

testBeforeApproval.how: Create the app and use it without submitting for review

source.quote: If you're building an internal tool or testing your integration, you can create and use an OAuth app without submitting it for review.
tasks:read - View basic task information like name and assignee
users:read - Access user information like email and profile picture

blockers.summary: Requesting a scope that is not registered on the app gives a forbidden_scopes error on the authorization page

source.quote: If you request a scope that is not in your app's approved (i.e., registered) list, the user will see a forbidden_scopes error on the authorization page.

blockers.summary: Scopes do not exist for every endpoint, so some apps must switch on Full permissions

source.quote: scopes are not yet available for every Asana API endpoint

blockers.summary: Apps built with app components go through a security review and QA before they are listed in the app gallery

source.quote: if your app uses app components your submission will go through a security review and QA process before it's listed in the in-product app gallery

blockers.summary: After a submission for review, the app can no longer be edited

source.quote: At this point, the app will no longer be open for further edits.

avoidProducts.name: Asana MCP apps
avoidProducts.why: MCP apps are a separate app type that does not use OAuth scopes
avoidProducts.evidence: Appeared in web search results for the Asana OAuth docs (2026-10-29)

notes: Asana's older pages describe a small default scope set and app creation under account settings; the current docs use the developer console and resource:action scopes. The golden set follows the current docs.
